content.thinking:
Let me analyze this certificate.

Certificate:
- Number: R60/2017-A-NL1-22.18, revision 0
- Scheme: A
- Project number: 3548307
- Page total: 3
- Member state: The Netherlands
- Date issued: 1 September 2022
- OIML issuer ID: NL1

Issuing authority:
- Name: NMi Certin B.V. (OIML Issuing Authority NL1)
- Address: Thijsweg 11, 2629 JA Delft, The Netherlands
- Person responsible: M.Ph.D. Schmidt
- Phone: +31 88 6362332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl
- oiml_issuer_id: NL1

Applicant and Manufacturer: PAVONE SISTEMI, S.R.L., VIA TIBERIO BIANCHI 11/13/15, 20863 – CONCOREZZO (MB), ITALY

Certified type:
- Category: Load cell
- Type designations: BBR, BBF
- Trade name: UTILCELL
- Module designation: "Analog passive load cell"
- Description: bending beam load cell with strain gauges

Model family: The Emax column shows three ranges: "5 kg up to 30 kg", "30 kg up to 100 kg", "100 kg up to and including 500 kg". The n (max load cell intervals) varies per column: 4000, 3000, 4000. So this is a model-level matrix with 3 capacity ranges.

So model_family models:
- model_id: "Emax=5-30kg"? Actually the columns are capacity ranges. Let me define models:
  - "Emax=5-30kg" (label "5 kg up to 30 kg")
  - "Emax=30-100kg"
  - "Emax=100-500kg"

Model-level characteristics:
- maximum_capacity ranges per model... Actually max capacity is the range itself. I could record "maximum_capacity" per model with min/max values in kg.
- max_number_of_load_cell_intervals_nlc (n): 4000, 3000, 4000 — footnote 1.

Type-level characteristics:
- minimum_dead_load: 0 kg
- accuracy_class: C
- rated_output: 2 mV/V ± 0.1 mV/V — this has value + tolerance. Value: 2, unit: mV/V, with tolerance 0.1 mV/V. Hmm. Structured shape only allows value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. Maybe represent value as string "2 ± 0.1" or as an object? Rules say value can be number | {min,max} | string. I'll use value: "2 ± 0.1", unit_symbol: "mV/V". Alternatively record rated_output_nominal: 2, rated_output_tolerance: 0.1. Simpler: value "2 ± 0.1" mV/V. But rule says numbers not strings... The ± form is not a simple number; a range interpretation could be {min: 1.9, max: 2.1} but that changes meaning slightly (it is actually a tolerance band). I think it's acceptable to record as value: {min: 1.9, max: 2.1}? Hmm, that would be fabricating interpretation. Rated output 2 mV/V ± 0.1 mV/V means nominal 2 with tolerance ±0.1. I'll keep value as string "2 ± 0.1" with unit mV/V. Actually maybe better to split: rated_output: {value: 2, unit_symbol: "mV/V"}, rated_output_tolerance: {value: 0.1, unit_symbol: "mV/V"}. That's clean and numeric. I'll do that.
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 20000 (footnote 1)
- ratio_z_emax_over_2dr: 4000 (footnote 1)
- input_impedance: 400 Ω ± 20 Ω → nominal 400, tolerance 20. Similar approach: input_impedance: 400 Ω, input_impedance_tolerance: 20 Ω. Or keep string. I'll split similarly.
- temperature_range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40} °C
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7 (converted from 0,7)
- humidity_class: CH
- safe_overload: 200 % of Emax → value 200, unit %, plus safe_overload_reference: "Emax"
- output_impedance: 350 Ω ± 3 Ω → 350, tolerance 3
- recommended_excitation: 10 V AC/DC → value 10, unit V, and excitation_type? The rule example: `110-240V AC 50/60Hz` splits into voltage, frequency, type. Here "10 V AC / DC" — value 10 V, type "AC / DC". I'll record recommended_excitation: 10 V and recommended_excitation_type: "AC / DC".
- excitation_maximum: 15 V AC/DC → same.
- transducer_material: Stainless steel
- atmospheric_protection: Hermetically sealed/welded

Characterization: "Analog passive load cell" — module_designation.

Recommendation: R60, edition 2017, scheme A, accuracy_classes ["C"].

Test reports:
- NMi-2309247-01 rev 1, 4 February 2020, 52 pages, role: type_evaluation_report
- NMi-2309247-02, 4 September 2019, 24 pages, role: type_evaluation_report
- NMi-2309247-03, 4 September 2019, 24 pages, role: type_evaluation_report

Revision history: revision "0", 1 September 2022, "Initial issue."

Footnotes: marker "1)", text "The characteristics for n_max, Y and Z can be reduced separately." Actually the remark says: "The characteristics for nmax, Y and Z can be reduced separately." That is footnote (1) attached to n, Y, Z rows.

Also national requirements: US NIST Handbook 44, NCWM Publication 14, accuracy class III L. Should I record? Maybe in a note or additional field. The schema doesn't have a slot; could put in description or omit. I might add to characteristics type_level? No — better omit or include in description. I could add a "national_requirements" note inside description or omit. Rules say don't fabricate; there's no field. I'll skip it, or possibly include in description text. Description is "free-text description if present" — the description present is "A bending beam load cell, with strain gauges." Keep that.

Now model_level entries:

1. maximum_capacity per model: values as {min,max} ranges in kg:
   - model "Emax=5-30kg": {min: 5, max: 30}? Actually the column header is "5 kg up to 30 kg" meaning capacity range for that model group. I'll record maximum_capacity with value {min:5, max:30} kg etc.
2. max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: 4000, 3000, 4000 with footnote_markers ["1)"].

Model IDs: Let me name them "BBR/BBF 5–30 kg"? Better neutral: "Emax=5kg-30kg", "Emax=30kg-100kg", "Emax=100kg-500kg". I'll use those.

matrix_tables: I could include the characteristics table as a matrix table too. The instructions for R60 example only require model_family + model_level. I could also add matrix_tables entry capturing the full table. It says preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. The table mostly fits into type_level + model_level. I'll include one matrix_table for the characteristics table to be safe? It might be redundant. I think it's fine to include it for fidelity. Hmm — but schema example for R137 shows matrix_tables AND model_level. For R60 example, only model_level shown. I'll include matrix_tables too, capturing the raw table with columns.

Actually let me keep it clean: include matrix_tables with the characteristics table, columns: characteristic, unit?, range columns. The table structure: first row is "Characterization ... | Analog passive load cell". Second row: Emax with three range columns. Third: minimum dead load (colspan 3). etc. Modeling that as a matrix table is awkward. I'll skip matrix_tables since data fits type/model level, per R60 example. Actually rule 4 for R60 doesn't include matrix_tables. I'll follow R60 example.

Footnote markers: The table uses ^{(1)} — marker "1)". Footnotes array: marker "1)", text as given.

Now assemble JSON.

certificate:
{
  "number": "R60/2017-A-NL1-22.18",
  "scheme": "A",
  "project_number": "3548307",
  "page_total": 3,
  "member_state": "The Netherlands",
  "date_issued": "2022-09-01",
  "oiml_issuer_id": "NL1"
}

Should date be ISO? Probably fine either way; I'll use "2022-09-01".

issuing_authority:
{
  "name": "NMi Certin B.V.",
  "address_lines": ["Thijsweg 11", "2629 JA Delft", "The Netherlands"],
  "person_responsible": "M.Ph.D. Schmidt",
  "phone": "+31 88 6362332",
  "email": "certin@nmi.nl",
  "website": "www.nmi.nl",
  "oiml_issuer_id": "NL1"
}

applicants: [{name: "PAVONE SISTEMI, S.R.L.", address_lines: ["VIA TIBERIO BIANCHI 11/13/15", "20863 – CONCOREZZO (MB)", "ITALY"]}]

manufacturers: same.

certified_type:
{
  "category": "Load cell",
  "type_designations": ["BBR", "BBF"],
  "module_designation": "Analog passive load cell",
  "description": "Bending beam load cell with strain gauges. Registered trade name: UTILCELL."
}

Maybe add trade_name? Not in schema; put in description.

model_family:
{
  "family_name": "UTILCELL",
  "models": [
    {"model_id": "Emax=5-30kg", "label": "5 kg up to 30 kg", "attributes": {}},
    ...
  ]
}

Family name: UTILCELL is a registered trade name, could be family name. I'll set family_name to "UTILCELL" — it's explicit-ish ("Registered trade name: UTILCELL"). Acceptable.

Type-level characteristics — each value structured:
- minimum_dead_load: {value: 0, unit_symbol: "kg", unit_id: null}
- accuracy_class: {value: "C", ...} — unit null.
- rated_output: {value: 2, unit_symbol: "mV/V"}
- rated_output_tolerance: {value: 0.1, unit_symbol: "mV/V"}
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: {value: 20000, footnote_markers: ["1)"]}
- ratio_z_emax_over_2dr: {value: 4000, footnote_markers: ["1)"]}
- input_impedance: {value: 400, unit_symbol: "Ω"}
- input_impedance_tolerance: {value: 20, unit_symbol: "Ω"}
- output_impedance: {value: 350, unit_symbol: "Ω"}
- output_impedance_tolerance: {value: 3, unit_symbol: "Ω"}
- temperature_range: {value: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit_symbol: "°C"}
- apportionment_factor_plc: {value: 0.7}
- humidity_class: {value: "CH"}
- safe_overload: {value: 200, unit_symbol: "%"}
- safe_overload_reference: {value: "Emax"}
- recommended_excitation: {value: 10, unit_symbol: "V"}
- recommended_excitation_type: {value: "AC / DC"}
- excitation_maximum: {value: 15, unit_symbol: "V"}
- excitation_maximum_type: {value: "AC / DC"}
- transducer_material: {value: "Stainless steel"}
- atmospheric_protection: {value: "Hermetically sealed/welded"}

Model-level:
- maximum_capacity: values per model {min,max} kg
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: per model, footnote ["1)"]

Model-level values shape: {"model": ..., "value": ..., "footnote_markers": [...]} — the schema example shows {"model": "Emax=25t", "value": 25} without unit; unit at attribute level (unit_symbol). For max capacity ranges, value is {min,max}. OK.

recommendation:
{
  "id": "R60",
  "edition": 2017,
  "amendment": null,
  "scheme": "A",
  "accuracy_classes": ["C"]
}

test_reports: role — the reports are the Type Evaluation Report(s). role: "type_evaluation_report".

revision_history: [{revision: "0", date: "2022-09-01", changes: "Initial issue."}]

footnotes: [{marker: "1)", text: "The characteristics for nmax, Y and Z can be reduced separately."}]

Also "Remark: 1." — yes.

Double-check decimal: "0,7" → 0.7 ✓. "± 0,1 mV/V" → 0.1 ✓.

Output JSON without fences.
